description: Answers to a player's asks and questions: groups, help, where/what, frontier, great hunts, battlegrounds, trade, dungeons, and a general fallback.

lines.text: I could join you, {player}, once I am done with {target}.
Try the camps around {zone}. Groups gather there often.
What do you need, {player}? Ask away.
I am headed to {destination} myself, {player}. Follow the road signs.
Good question. Your trainer can tell you more than I can.
The frontier is restless. Bring friends if you go.
Great hunts are called at the Horn of Rallying. Keep an ear out for it.
The battlegrounds are a good place to learn the frontier before the real thing.
The Realm Exchange is the place to start, {player}.
Dungeons go best with a full group and a careful puller.
Fair enough, {player}.
What level are you, {player}? Hard to point you anywhere without knowing.
Which class, {player}? Groups are always short a healer or a tank.
Tied up with {target} for now. Ask me again after.
Could use a hand myself once {target} is down, {player}.
Put your level and class in realm chat. Someone usually bites.
Groups form fast near the busier camps around {zone}.
Healers never wait long for a group. The rest of us wait a bit.
Mine is full right now, sorry {player}.
We might have a spot opening soon. No promises though.
Sit near the zone line and call out. Folk pass through all the time.
If you can tank, {player}, you will have a group in no time.
Not grouped myself at the moment. Could be worth teaming up later, {player}.
Depends on your level. The camps here suit some better than others.
Plenty of soloers in {zone} right now. Some of them might want company.
Have you tried your guild first, {player}?
Small groups do fine out here. Two or three is plenty for most camps.
lfg is slow right now. Hang in there.
A crowd near a dungeon entrance usually means a group is forming.
Bards and druids get snapped up quickly. Lucky them.
Clerics and friars get invited before they finish asking.
Healers and shamans get scooped up quick around here.
Bring a few potions, {player}, and you will be welcome in most groups.
We need a puller more than anything. Can you pull, {player}?
Give me a moment to finish {target}, then we can see.
Heading to {destination} first. Maybe after that, {player}.
No room just now, {player}, but keep asking. Groups break up often.
When nobody answers, try a different zone for a while.
Most groups want someone within a few levels of them.
Tell folk what you bring to a group, {player}. It helps more than you would think.
Once folk hit their thirties they drift toward the dungeons.
The forties crowd gathers for Darkness Falls whenever the realm holds it.
If I had a spot, it would be yours, {player}.
Grouping is the fastest way up. Soloing gets slow past the twenties.
Anyone in the guild free for {player}? They want a group.
What is your role, {player}? Damage, heals, or crowd control?
Casters are always welcome if they can mez or root, {player}.
Crowd control is worth its weight in gold in a group.
Stick around, {player}. The evening crowd brings more groups.
A level or two of soloing first never hurt anyone.
Not looking for more right now, but good luck, {player}.
Stealthers have it rough finding groups. The frontier suits them better.
Archers make fine pullers, if that is what you play.
Wander over to the nearest camp and ask. Someone always needs one more.
Look for the bigger campfires. That is where the groups rest.
Grouped already, but my friends might want company later.
Hard to find a group this early, {player}. Give it a little time.
Low levels do well around Cotswold and the Camelot Hills.
Mularn and the fields around it are busy with new folk looking for groups.
Mag Mell and Tir na mBeo are good places to find others starting out.
Ugh, I know the feeling. Took me ages to find my last group.
Sounds like you need a group, {player}. Keep shouting, it works.
Sure, {player}. What is the trouble?
Happy to help if I can. What is going on?
What are you stuck on, {player}?
Need directions, a group, or something else?
If you go down near me, {player}, I will try to get to you.
No promises, but if I see you fall I will try for a rez.
Quest givers often have more to say if you speak to them again.
Lost, {player}? Find a road and follow it. Roads lead to towns.
Short on coin? Sell your loot to a merchant before you buy anything.
Low on health, {player}? Sit and rest a moment before the next pull.
Always carry a few potions. They have saved me more than once.
Watch your con colors, {player}. Anything red or purple will flatten you.
Blue and yellow cons are the sweet spot for solo hunting.
Died and lost experience? Pray at your gravestone to win some back.
Bind somewhere close to where you hunt, {player}. Saves a long walk.
Visit your trainer each level. Easy to forget.
Keep your gear repaired, {player}. A smith can fix it up for you.
Stuck in the scenery? Try /stuck, it has saved me before.
Pull one at a time, {player}. The second add is what gets you.
Fighting near the guards helps. They do not like monsters in town.
Tell me more, {player}. I will help if I can.
Hold on, {player}. Let me finish {target} and I am all ears.
Busy with {target} right now, but ask away.
On my way to {destination}, but I can answer a question or two.
Overloaded? Drop the junk. Moving slowly gets you killed.
Running out of power? Sit down and let it come back before the next fight.
Do not panic, {player}. Most trouble looks worse than it is.
Rough day, {player}? We have all been there.
Something keeps killing you? Try a different camp for a while.
Pet class? Let the pet take the hits and keep your distance.
Casters should stand back and let the tank grab attention first.
No shame in asking. Everyone was new once, {player}.
What zone are you in, {player}? That changes the answer.
Grey con monsters give nothing. Save your time for blue and up.
Yell if you need a hand, {player}. Folk around here look out for each other.
Badly lost? Head back toward Camelot and start fresh.
Lost in the snow? The roads back to Jordheim are well travelled.
When all else fails, make your way back to Tir na Nog and ask there.
Went down? Release and come back. Your gravestone will wait.
Wait for full health and power before every pull. Patience saves lives.
Stay out of the worst of it, {player}. Heals only stretch so far.
My heals are not much, but I will throw a few your way if I am close.
Keep your back to a wall when things get hairy. Fewer surprises.
Speak up, {player}. Nobody minds a question.
First thing: breathe. Second thing: what happened?
Follow the road signs, {player}. They rarely lie.
A stable master can get you there faster than walking, {player}.
Head for the nearest town and ask the stable master about routes.
Going to {destination} myself. Might be the same road.
Not sure, {player}. Ask a guard. They know the area well.
Guards point the way if you ask them nicely, {player}.
Check your map, {player}. The towns are marked.
It is out there somewhere. Realm chat might have exact directions.
Never been there myself, sorry {player}.
Stick to the roads, {player}. Cutting across country gets folk killed.
Horses leave from the stables in most towns. Easier on the boots.
The roads fork a lot, {player}. Read every signpost.
Merchants know the roads better than anyone. Ask one.
Head toward {destination} and ask again from there.
Walking to {destination} myself. You could tag along part of the way.
Not far, I think. Then again, everything is far on foot.
The border keeps are the way into the frontier. A horse gets you most of the way.
Most horse routes run out of Camelot and the towns along the main road.
Hadrian's Wall is where our frontier starts. Go with friends.
Odin's Gate is where our frontier starts. Take company.
Emain Macha is where our frontier starts. Bring a group.
From Jordheim you can catch a horse to most of the big towns.
Tir na Nog has stable masters who can send you most places.
For the isles, ask around town. There is always a way across.
Guards hear all the stories. Ask one where the nearest dungeon is.
It is marked on most maps, {player}. Have a look at yours.
Bit of a walk from here. Grab a horse ticket if you can.
Buy a ticket from the stable master and enjoy the ride, {player}.
No idea, {player}. I get lost myself half the time.
Realm chat will know the way. Someone always does.
Find the zone line and keep going. You will know it when you see it.
Depends where you are starting from, {player}.
Bind at the town nearest your hunting spot. Walking back after a death is no fun.
Guards and a merchant? Then you have found a town, at least.
Would point you there, but {target} needs my attention first.
Down the road and keep asking, {player}. That is how I find anything.
Look for the signpost at the crossroads, {player}.
Dungeon entrances usually have a few adventurers camped outside. Look for them.
The Shrouded Isles are worth the trip once you are a little stronger.
Anyone near the bindstone can point you to a good hunting spot for your level.
Which part are you after, {player}? The town or the hunting grounds?
Couple of zones over, I believe. Ask a guard when you get closer.
Ask any guard in Mularn or Audliten. They point new folk the right way.
The guards in Mag Mell and Ardee know these roads well.
Cotswold and Ludlow guards can set you on the right road.
Ask your trainer, {player}. That is what they are there for.
Hard to say, {player}. Every class plays it a little differently.
No idea, honestly. Try asking in realm chat.
Guards know a lot more than they let on. Try one.
Good question, {player}. I have wondered that myself.
Some say one thing, some say another. Try it and see.
Trainers explain skills best. Mine set me straight more than once.
That depends on your class, {player}.
Not sure. An older hand in your guild might know.
Quest givers in town will explain it if you speak to them again.
Delve it and see what it says, {player}.
Merchants will buy almost anything. Sell what you do not need.
Worth a try, {player}. Worst case, you learn something.
Heard the same rumour. No idea if it is true.
That one is beyond me, {player}. Sorry.
Ask me something easier, like where the nearest merchant is.
Specs are a matter of taste, {player}. Pick what fits how you like to play.
Realm points come from the frontier. Fighting the enemy, taking keeps.
Con color tells you a lot. Green is easy, red is trouble.
Most of it comes down to patience and a good group.
You will figure it out, {player}. We all did, mostly.
Give me a moment, {player}. {target} has my full attention.
Walking to {destination}, so short answer: ask a guard.
That is a question for a trainer, not a {class} like me.
Even after all these levels I learn something new each day.
Honestly? I just hit things until they stop moving.
Ask a crafter. They know materials inside and out.
Depends who you ask, {player}. Everyone has a theory.
Sounds like a rumour to me. Plenty of those going around.
Heard of it, {player}, but never seen it myself.
It is real enough. Just not something I have tried.
Older folk say it was always like that.
Have you checked with the guards? They hear everything.
Most townsfolk will chat if you speak to them. Try a few.
Sounds like you are due a trainer visit, {player}.
It is all in how you spec and how you play.
Dyes and such come from merchants in the bigger towns.
The trainers in Camelot have answers for most things.
The trainers in Jordheim know their business. Try them.
Trainers in Tir na Nog have seen it all. Ask them.
Quests? Look for folk in town with something to say. Many have work.
Experience comes faster in a group. That much I know for sure.
Good luck figuring that one out. Tell me if you do.
My {class} training never covered that, {player}.
Not a clue, {player}. I would ask an old hand.
The frontier is no place to go alone, {player}.
Darkness Falls only opens to the realm holding the most keeps. Watch them.
{enemyrealm} has been pushing hard lately. Be careful out there.
Take a horse to the border keep and go from there, {player}.
Small groups hunt the milegates. Big groups hit the keeps.
Realm points come easier in a group. Solo is a quick trip back to bind.
Stealthers lurk near the roads in the frontier. Keep moving.
Too low and you just feed realm points to {enemyrealm}. Level a bit first.
Relics are worth defending. Losing one hurts the whole realm.
Keep an eye on realm chat for keep warnings, {player}.
Join a guild that runs the frontier, {player}. It makes all the difference.
Everyone protects the healer out there. Remember that.
Never chase into their lines, {player}. That is how groups wipe.
The frontier is quiet one hour, chaos the next.
Tied up with {target}, but I would love a frontier run later.
Ready when the realm is, {player}.
Count me in for a defense. Attacks, maybe.
{enemyrealm} likes to camp the roads. Travel in a group.
Taking a keep takes patience. Doors first, then the lord.
Defending is easier than attacking. Grab the high ground on the walls.
Archers on the walls win more defenses than you would think.
Speed and a tight group. That is how you survive out there.
Hear inc in realm chat? Head for the keep.
Hadrian's Wall never stays quiet. The milegates take a beating.
Odin's Gate never stays quiet for long. Bring friends and a healer.
Emain Macha is where the fights are. Go with a group and stay together.
Guard the Scabbard and the Staff. Excalibur and Myrddin must not fall.
Thor's Hammer and the Horn of Valhalla stay in Midgard if I have any say.
Lug's Spear and the Cauldron of Dagda belong in Hibernia. Never forget it.
Go on, {player}. The realm needs every sword.
{enemyrealm} never fights fair, or so they say about us too.
Get a few more levels first, {player}. The frontier is unforgiving.
Battlegrounds first, frontier later. That is my advice, {player}.
Want to help the realm? Show up for keep defenses. Every body counts.
Bring siege help if you mean to take a keep. Rams do not build themselves.
When the Horn of Rallying sounds, drop what you are doing and join in.
Great hunts need numbers, {player}. Bring friends.
Dragon hunts need the whole realm, not just one guild.
Golestandt is no joke. Bring every healer you can find.
Gjalpinulva has flattened bigger raids than ours. Be ready for the run back.
Cuuldurach needs a full raid and steady nerves. Sit tight for the call.
Would join a hunt once I am done with {target}.
Count me in next time the Horn sounds, {player}.
Raids are mostly waiting, then a lot of shouting, then loot. I love them.
Stay with the main group, {player}. Stragglers get eaten.
Healers stand back, tanks stand forward, everyone listens to the leader.
Missed the last hunt. Hoping to catch the next one.
Great hunts go better when everyone is close to the right level.
Big monsters, big rewards. Worth the effort.
Bring potions and patience, {player}. Hunts can take a while.
Too low for it? Stay back and cheer. Someone has to.
Boss fights are chaos. Follow the leader and do not chase.
Last hunt I joined, we wiped twice before we got it.
A great hunt is the best way to see the whole realm work together.
The Horn has been quiet lately. Someone will sound it soon enough.
Legion in Darkness Falls makes for a long night. Bring your best.
Raids need organizing. Group up first, then join the hunt.
Ask around for the next hunt, {player}. Word travels fast.
Always up for a great hunt, {player}. Just say when.
Caer Sidi is a raid all on its own. Bring a full force.
Tuscaran Glacier is best done with a full force. Many have tried with less.
Galladoria is a long haul. Gather a full force before you go in.
If the raid wipes, release and run back, {player}. Do not give up.
Keep realm chat open. That is where hunts get called.
A few more for the hunt? I can ask around once {target} is down.
Abermenai is for levels 15 to 19. Dun Abermenai is the keep to hold.
At 20 to 24 you want Thidranki. Thidranki Faste is the prize.
Murdaigean covers 25 to 29. Fight for Dun Murdaigean.
Caledonia takes 30 to 35. Caer Caledon is the keep there.
What level are you, {player}? The battleground depends on it.
Battlegrounds are great practice. Low stakes, lots of fighting.
Outlevel a battleground and it sends you packing. Move up to the next.
Thidranki is always lively. Bring a healer.
Battlegrounds teach you to keep your head in a crowd.
Group up before you go in, {player}. Solos get picked off fast.
Take the keep and hold it. That is the whole game.
A guard can tell you the way into the battlegrounds.
Great place to earn your first realm points, {player}.
Bring friends your level, {player}. It makes all the difference in there.
Caledonia gets serious. Those folk know what they are doing.
Abermenai is a fine first taste of fighting {enemyrealm}.
Spent half my twenties in Thidranki. Good times.
Murdaigean is where people start to get clever with tactics.
Too high for the battlegrounds now, sadly. I miss them.
Thinking of a battleground run myself after {target}.
Watch out for {enemyrealm} archers on the keep walls.
Battlegrounds are good for learning your class against thinking foes.
Keep fell? Regroup and take it back. It changes hands all the time.
In there, stick to your group like glue, {player}.
Do not rush the keep alone. Wait for the group.
Caer Caledon is a tough nut to crack. Bring siege help.
Battlegrounds, {player}? Go for it. Best fun you can have at your level.
Brackets are strict, {player}. Check your level before you head in.
Practice there before the real frontier. You will thank yourself.
Under fifteen? Then the battlegrounds will have to wait, {player}.
Try the Realm Exchange first. Shop around before you buy.
A crafter might make it for you, {player}. Ask in realm chat.
Sell your loot to any merchant if nobody wants it.
Not selling anything right now, {player}, sorry.
Could use some coin myself, honestly.
Crafters always want materials. Ask what they need.
Spellcrafters can add a lot to plain gear. Worth looking into.
Hold on to anything that looks rare, {player}. It might be worth more than you think.
Guild crafters often do favours for friends.
Merchants in the bigger towns carry better stock.
Carrying nothing worth trading, {player}.
Never hand over the goods before the coin, {player}.
Armor from a good crafter beats most drops at your level.
Look for high quality pieces from crafters. Quality matters.
Weapons wear out. Find a smith who can repair them.
Shop around before you spend, {player}.
Saving up for a new weapon myself.
Checked the Realm Exchange lately? Things move fast there.
Selling to a merchant is quick. Trading takes patience.
Dyes, arrows, potions. Merchants have the basics covered.
Busy with {target} at the moment. Trade talk later, {player}.
Nothing to spare right now. Ask again later.
Alchemists can sort you out with potions if you ask.
Tailors and armorcrafters can fit you out better than any merchant.
Fair trades only, {player}. Keep that in mind.
Full group, a healer, and a steady hand. That is how you do a dungeon.
Pull carefully, {player}. Dungeons punish mistakes.
Take a puller who knows the place, {player}. It saves a lot of deaths.
Most dungeons have folk camped outside. Group up there.
Tomb of Mithra and Keltoi Fogou are good for newer folk.
Stonehenge Barrows is a big step up. Go with friends.
Krondon and Avalon City are rough. Only go with a strong group.
The Cursed Tomb is a fine first dungeon. Spindelhalla comes later.
Varulvhamn is full of werewolves. Bring a group that can take a beating.
Trollheim and Iarnvidiur's Lair are no place for the faint of heart.
Muire Tomb and the Spraggon Den are good places to start.
Coruscating Mine is a step up. Go in with a full group.
Tur Suil and Fomor are rough going. Bring your best.
In the middle of {target} here, but dungeons are always worth it.
Darkness Falls is the big one, when the realm holds it.
Darkness Falls is where I spend most evenings now.
Dungeon monsters hit harder than the ones outside. Respect them, {player}.
Check what level a dungeon suits before going in. Guards often know.
Corners are dangerous. Something is always waiting around one.
Mind the wanderers, {player}. They walk right into your pulls.
Bind nearby if you can. The run back after a wipe is long.
I like dungeons. No {enemyrealm} stealthers, just honest monsters.
Is your group ready, {player}? Dungeons are no place to wing it.
Heading to {destination} first, then maybe a dungeon run.
Group wiped? Wait for a rez before you release, if a healer is up.
Hmm, could be, {player}.
Cannot argue with that.
Interesting thought.
Maybe so. Time will tell.
Good point, {player}.
I hear you, {player}.
Not sure what to say to that, {player}.
Let me think on that one.
True enough, {player}.
Ha, fair.
Could be worse, {player}. Could be raining.
If you say so, {player}.
Agreed, mostly.
Well, that is one way to look at it.
Sounds about right to me.
Hard to say, {player}.
Noted, {player}. Thanks.
Right you are.
Busy with {target}, but I am listening.
On my way to {destination}, but go on.
